newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slightly stronger in moderate trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slightly stronger in moderate trade.

text.p: Irish bonds strengthened in moderate trade on Monday in line with a slight improvement in tone among international markets, dealers said.
"Markets seem to be doing quite well in Europe today and we've seen a reasonable amount of selling on the Irish market," a dealer said. "Spreads are continuing to narrow marginally."
Signals at the weekend of a softening in Germany's stance on the EMU entry criteria have been helpful, particularly to peripheral markets.
On Wednesday, bunds tested the top-side of their recent range, following Treasuries higher in the absence of any meaningful domestic news.
On the Irish market the 10-year spread over bunds in afternoon trading was at 91 basis points, while the five-year pick-up was at 146 basis points, dealers said.
Looking ahead to next Tuesday's NTMA auction of 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent Treasury bond due 2006, dealers said they expected reasonable domestic interest and some foreign demand.

"Today we've seen some switching and preparation activity ahead of the auction," a dealer said. "The bond is relatively cheap on the curve so we'll see domestic appetite anyway - the extent of foreign interest depends on sentiment in Europe and for the timebeing there's nothing too negative in the short term."

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up five pence from Tuesday's close at 101.68 to yield 6.05 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 12 pence from the close at 108.15 to yield 6.78 percent.
Dealers said the market would examine carefully Irish March consumer prices data due on Thursday.
Also, with worries about the possibility of higher U.S. interest rates continuing to undermine market sentiment, the release of U.S. March retail sales figures on Friday would be watched closely.
